If you had told me a year ago that Conservatives, [Conservatives from Alberta no less](http://globalnews.ca/news/2477657/alberta-tories-call-for-removal-of-same-sex-marriage-ban-in-party-policy/), would front a motion calling for a reversal of party policy regarding same sex marriage I probably would have chuckled politely and said it would never happen - but it did.

*Not only that,* but if you had told me that the leader of the Conservative Party of Canada would back such a call I would have LOL'd ... seriously, I would have LOL'd - [and yet that has happened as well](http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/rona-ambrose-same-sex-marriage-ban-1.3420219).

>Interim Conservative Leader Rona Ambrose says she backs a call for removal of the long-standing same-sex marriage ban from official Tory policy, her latest move to reshape the party in the post-Stephen Harper era.

>"I've been clear for a long time that the Conservative Party welcomes all conservatives, regardless of sexual orientation. If you believe in smaller government, lower taxes, balanced budgets and individual freedom, we want you in our party," Ambrose said in a statement to CBC News.

Time, and the May 2017 CPC leadership convention, will tell whether we're seeing the realization that Reform Party based social conservatism simply does not resonate with either modern Canadians or the majority of card carrying **C**onservatives - or whether this apparent progressive conservative movement will be crushed by party traditionalists.

On one side of the coin we would likely see a renewed party that stands a decent chance of a return to power, on the other a large national sigh - followed by, "*yup, we knew it, they really are a bunch of knuckle dragging has-beens from a long passed era*"

Personally I'm going to hope that the CPC *does* bring itself into the 21st century.
